question: What is the primary objective of the disinfection process in a healthcare facility?

options.A: To completely eliminate all bacterial spores
options.B: To sterilize surgical instruments for immediate use
options.C: To reduce pathogens on inanimate objects to safe levels
options.D: To remove organic soil from human skin surfaces

explanation: Disinfection focuses on lowering the microbial load on inanimate surfaces rather than achieving total sterility. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h1)

question: Why is it clinically incorrect to refer to a disinfected surface as sterile?

options.A: Disinfection destroys vegetative bacteria but often leaves behind resistant spores
options.B: Sterile items are restricted exclusively to operating theatre environments
options.C: Disinfected surfaces always retain a thin layer of chemical residue
options.D: Sterilization can only be performed using physical methods like boiling water

explanation: Sterilization requires the complete destruction of all forms of microbial life, including highly resistant bacterial endospores, which standard disinfection does not achieve. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h1)

question: Which level of disinfection is required to inactivate Mycobacterium tuberculosis?
explanation: Mycobacterium tuberculosis serves as the benchmark organism for intermediate-level disinfectants, proving their potency against tough, non-lipid vegetative pathogens. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h2)

question: A student nurse is preparing a chemical bath for semi-critical instruments that touch mucous membranes. Which performance tier must the chosen disinfectant achieve?
explanation: Semi-critical items require high-level disinfection because they come into contact with non-intact skin or mucous membranes and need virtually all microbial life eliminated short of high spore counts. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h2)

question: Which process is specifically designed to be safe for application on living human tissue?
explanation: Antiseptics are chemical agents formulated specifically for use on skin and living tissues to reduce infection risks without causing severe cellular damage. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h3)

question: What is the primary operational difference between decontamination and sterilization?

options.A: Sterilization is the first step before any physical cleaning can take place
options.B: Decontamination uses chemical agents exclusively, whereas sterilization uses heat
options.C: Decontamination removes dirt and pathogens, while sterilization achieves total microbial eradication
options.D: Sterilization can only be performed in hospital laboratories, unlike decontamination

explanation: Decontamination makes an item safe by cleaning away organic matter and reducing hazards, whereas sterilization eliminates every single microbial entity present. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h3)

question: Which chemical compound is most commonly prepared daily for cleaning blood spills on hospital floors?
explanation: Chlorine-releasing agents like sodium hypochlorite are the standard choice for blood and body fluid spill management because they rapidly inactivate bloodborne pathogens. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h4)

question: A ward nurse notes that alcohol-based surface wipes evaporate quickly without leaving a film. What is a key practical limitation of this property?

options.A: They damage stainless steel medical instruments instantly
options.B: They cannot kill any vegetative bacteria
options.C: They require high temperatures to activate their ingredients
options.D: They lack residual antimicrobial action on the surface

explanation: Because alcohols evaporate quickly, they do not leave behind a persistent chemical residue to prevent subsequent microbial contamination. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h4)

question: What is the primary reason for thoroughly washing a dirty instrument before applying a chemical disinfectant?

options.A: Water speeds up the evaporation rate of the disinfectant
options.B: Soap enhances the pleasant fragrance of the disinfectant
options.C: Washing prevents the metal from rusting during disinfection
options.D: Organic matter can shield microbes and neutralize the chemical agent

explanation: Organic material like blood or protein creates a physical barrier that protects underlying pathogens and inactivates many chemical disinfectants. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h5)

question: A nurse wipes a treatment trolley quickly with a disinfectant wipe, drying it immediately with a paper towel. What clinical mistake was made?

options.A: Using a low-level disinfectant on a critical item
options.B: Omitting the pre-cleaning soap wash stage
options.C: Ignoring the manufacturer's required contact time
options.D: Failing to use an alcohol-based solution

explanation: Disinfectants require a specific duration of uninterrupted wet contact time to successfully destroy target pathogens. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h5)

question: According to the Spaulding classification, what level of processing is required for a stethoscope touching intact skin?
explanation: Stethoscopes are classified as non-critical items because they only contact intact skin, requiring basic low-level disinfection between patients. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h6)

question: A nurse is reprocessing a flexible gastrointestinal endoscope after a diagnostic procedure. Based on the Spaulding system, how should this device be treated?

options.A: Wrapped in cloth and autoclaved at high heat
options.D: Cleaned with soap and water only

explanation: Endoscopes contact mucous membranes and are categorized as semi-critical devices, necessitating high-level disinfection to prevent cross-infection. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h6)

question: Why is the top-to-bottom cleaning technique strictly enforced during ward environmental disinfection?

options.A: It prevents staff from missing corners of the room during the shift
options.B: It allows the chemical solutions to evaporate faster on lower shelves
options.C: It ensures that dust and debris fall onto uncleaned areas to be wiped last
options.D: It reduces the physical exertion required by domestic cleaning staff

explanation: Gravity causes particles and contaminated debris to drop downward, meaning cleaning from high to low prevents newly cleaned surfaces from becoming soiled again. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h7)

question: Which group of hospital surfaces typically demands the highest frequency of routine cleaning and disinfection?

options.A: Storage shelves in the central supply room

explanation: Frequently touched items like bed rails and door handles harbor transient pathogens and require regular disinfection because hands touch them constantly. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h7)

question: What is the primary reason for wearing utility gloves and eye protection when diluting concentrated disinfectants?

options.A: To comply with fire safety regulations in the hospital
options.B: To prevent chemical splashes and skin irritation
options.C: To eliminate the need for hand hygiene afterwards
options.D: To maintain a sterile surgical field in the ward

explanation: Concentrated chemical disinfectants are caustic and can cause severe skin irritation, burns, or eye damage upon direct contact. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h8)

question: Which of the following actions is NOT recommended when handling chemical disinfectants in a clinical unit?

options.A: Mixing different chemical solutions together in a bucket to boost cleaning power
options.B: Ensuring the utility room has adequate ventilation during use
options.C: Checking the manufacturer instructions for proper dilution ratios
options.D: Wearing appropriate protective gear while wiping contaminated equipment

explanation: Mixing cleaning chemicals is dangerous because it can neutralize their active properties or release toxic, life-threatening gases such as chlorine fumes. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h8)
